newsitem.title: UK: Hong Kong stocks in London weak after HK drops.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks in London weak after HK drops.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks in London were mostly weaker on Monday, taking their cue from a sharp drop in Hong Kong after a wave of profit-taking.
The Hang Seng London Reference Index was down 7.78 points at 12,254.99 in mid-afternoon trade after the Hang Seng Index closed one percent lower, hit by a sell-off in property stocks.
Dealers said the string of key economic data from the U.S. this week was likely to keep Hong Kong stocks rangebound, chiefly Friday's U.S. payroll data.
In addition, next week's U.S. presidential election would encourage investors to play safe, dealers said.

"Turnover has been very low and people are going to sit on their hands. We could see some fun and games from this week's October futures expiry but other than that, we don't see much movement before Friday's figures," one dealer said.
The market weakened as HSBC Holdings reversed modest early gains to trade HK$0.40 lower at HK$156.75, dealers said. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 4367
